quran.note: Dhul-Kifl is named with Ismail and Idris among the patient and the righteous.
Dhul-Kifl is named with Ismail and Elisha among the outstanding.

scholarly.work: Ma’ariful Qur’an (English edition, read on Quran.com)
scholarly.author: Mufti Muhammad Shafi’
scholarly.summary: Records that Ibn Kathir thinks the mention beside the prophets shows he was a prophet, while others call him a pious man. Gives Mujahid’s report (through Ibn Jarir) that he was a deputy of Yasa’ who kept three conditions: fasting all year, praying all night, and not losing his temper. Says a Musnad Ahmad report from Ibn Umar about a man called “Kifl” is weak, is not in the six books and lacks “Dhul”, so it concerns someone else.

differences.question: Was Dhul-Kifl a prophet?

views.who: Ibn Kathir, as quoted in Ma’ariful Qur’an
views.work: Ma’ariful Qur’an (English edition, read on Quran.com), on 21:85
views.view: Yes; he is mentioned alongside prophets.

views.who: Others, as quoted in Ma’ariful Qur’an
views.work: Ma’ariful Qur’an (English edition, read on Quran.com), on 21:85
views.view: He was a pious man or saint, not a prophet.

differences.note: The Qur’an names him but tells no story. Everything about the three conditions comes from Mujahid, not from the Qur’an or a checked hadith.
